units.note: Whether ὁμολογουμένως ('admittedly') belongs to Timaeus's own words or is Polybius's gloss is uncertain; the English keeps it inside the quotation, which is defensible.

Final clause τὸ δὲ πολλὰ διαθέσθαι καὶ ματαίως τῶν ἐν μέσῳ κειμένων καὶ κοινόν: the Greek reads only 'common' (κοινόν). 'and easy' has no word behind it in this text. It may be an editor's supplement for a suspected gap, but no lacuna is marked here. No fix proposed; flagging for an editor to decide.

findings.quote: he says they had fixed their attention and learned how great a difference war makes from peace
findings.problem: λοιπόν φησιν αὐτοὺς ἐπιστήσαντας μαθεῖν ἡλίκην ὁ πόλεμος διαφορὰν ἔχει τῆς εἰρήνης: φησί + infinitive here is an exhortation, 'he tells them they must now attend and learn' how great the difference is. That is the absurdity Polybius points out: Hermocrates tells men he has just praised for knowing the difference that they must learn it. The current English makes it a statement of fact that they had already learned it, which takes the point away.
findings.proposed_fix: he tells them that they must now give their attention and learn how great a difference war makes from peace
